title: Be used to / get used to
note: PULLED FORWARD 2026-09-02 from the parked b2_be_get_used_to (bank was empty - auto-authored and removed 2026-08-29, do NOT refill from auto). be/get used to + -ing = zvyknout si. Two traps: the -ing (*I am used to work here) and be vs get (the state you are in vs the change into it). Kept clear of b1_used_to, which is WOULD for past habits. Thickened 10 -> 24 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop). Rules applied this pass: F4 was a false positive on She's - the subject contraction moved out of `en` and into accepts, which also cleared the two F3 leads (they're / she's); A8 closed the twins; A4 the cold became cold weather. C11: the contrast with a2_used_to (used to work / am used to working) had one mistakes row and no page - it now has a card of its own and a Quiz item whose options are the four real shapes. B1: the noise options were garbage (noise to be, hear noise) and now carry this unit's own error, the bare infinitive. Remaining lint: one A4 on `driving on the left`, where English forces the article, and vocablevel, which starts firing on any grammar pack once it has enough items to cross the check's 40-token floor - queued in DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Be used to / get used to
cards.title_cz: Be used to / get used to — zvyknout si
points: Czech **zvyknout si** covers both. English splits the state from the change.

rows: you are already comfortable with it
you are becoming comfortable with it

examples.en: She **got used** to the cold quickly.

cards.title: Always -ing
points: **to** in *used to* is a preposition, so a verb after it takes **-ing**.

rows: the state — it is normal for me
I **got used** to it last year.

cards.title: used to do, or be used to doing?
cards.title_cz: used to dělat, nebo be used to dělání?
points: The past habit is **used to** + plain verb.
How it feels now is *be* **used to** + -ing.

rows: a past habit — I do not now
it feels normal to me now

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: After **used to** here, a verb always takes **-ing**.

rows: ~~I am used to the cold weather get up early.~~
I am used to **getting** up early.
~~She is getting used to speak English.~~
She is getting used to **speaking** English.

blocks.title: Be used to / get used to · B1

items.en: I am used to working late.
items.cz: Jsem zvyklý pracovat pozdě.
items.gap: I am used to ____ late. (work)
accepts: I am used to working late.
I'm used to working late.
items.wrong: I am used to work late.
items.explanation: **be used to** takes **-ing**: used to **working**. Not the infinitive.
items.explanation_cz: **be used to** má **-ing**: used to **working**. Ne infinitiv.

items.en: She got used to cold weather quickly.
items.cz: Rychle si zvykla na chladné počasí.
items.gap: She ____ used to cold weather quickly. (get)
accepts: She got used to cold weather quickly.
items.explanation: **got** used to = the change happened. **was** used to would mean she already was.
items.explanation_cz: **got** used to = ta změna proběhla. **was** used to by znamenalo, že už zvyklá byla.
items.wrong: She is got used to cold weather quickly.

items.en: He isn't used to driving on the left.
items.cz: Není zvyklý jezdit vlevo.
items.gap: He isn't used to ____ on the left. (drive)
accepts: He isn't used to driving on the left.
He is not used to driving on the left.
items.wrong: He isn't used to drive on the left.
items.explanation: Still **-ing** after a negative: isn't used to **driving**.
items.explanation_cz: I po záporu zůstává **-ing**: isn't used to **driving**.

items.en: Are you used to the noise yet?
items.cz: Zvykl sis už na ten hluk?
items.gap: Are you used to ____ yet? (the noise)
accepts: Are you used to the noise yet?
items.explanation: A noun after **used to** stays as it is — only verbs take **-ing**.
items.explanation_cz: Podstatné jméno po **used to** zůstává, jak je — jen slovesa mají **-ing**.

items.en: I am getting used to my new job.
items.cz: Zvykám si na novou práci.
items.gap: I am ____ used to my new job. (get)
accepts: I am getting used to my new job.
I'm getting used to my new job.
items.explanation: The change is still happening, so **getting** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Změna pořád probíhá, takže **getting** used to.
items.wrong: I am get used to my new job.

items.en: They are used to getting up early.
items.cz: Jsou zvyklí vstávat brzy.
items.gap: They are used to ____ up early. (get)
accepts: They are used to getting up early.
They're used to getting up early.
items.wrong: They are used to get up early.
items.explanation: Two used-tos in one sentence is fine — the second verb still takes **-ing**.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě used to v jedné větě nevadí — druhé sloveso má pořád **-ing**.

items.en: It took me a month to get used to the food.
items.cz: Trvalo mi měsíc zvyknout si na to jídlo.
items.gap: It took me a month to ____ used to the food. (get)
accepts: It took me a month to get used to the food.
items.explanation: After **to** here you need the plain **get**: to get used to.
items.explanation_cz: Po **to** tady potřebuješ základní **get**: to get used to.

items.en: She is used to speaking English at work.
items.cz: Je zvyklá mluvit v práci anglicky.
items.gap: She is used to ____ English at work. (speak)
accepts: She is used to speaking English at work.
She's used to speaking English at work.
items.wrong: She is used to speak English at work.
items.explanation: **speaking** — the -ing form after used to.
items.explanation_cz: **speaking** — tvar s -ing po used to.

items.en: I can't get used to the weather here.
items.cz: Nemůžu si zvyknout na tady to počasí.
items.gap: I can't ____ used to the weather here. (get)
accepts: I can't get used to the weather here.
I cannot get used to the weather here.
items.explanation: After **can't** you need the plain verb: can't **get** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Po **can't** potřebuješ základní tvar: can't **get** used to.

items.en: We soon got used to living in a small flat.
items.cz: Brzy jsme si zvykli bydlet v malém bytě.
items.gap: We soon got used to ____ in a small flat. (live)
accepts: We soon got used to living in a small flat.
items.wrong: We soon got used to live in a small flat.
items.explanation: **got** used to marks the change, and **living** keeps the -ing.
items.explanation_cz: **got** used to značí změnu a **living** drží -ing.

items.en: I am not used to getting up at five.
items.cz: Nejsem zvyklý vstávat v pět.
items.gap: I am not used to ____ up at five. (get)
accepts: I am not used to getting up at five.
I'm not used to getting up at five.
items.wrong: I am not used to get up at five.
items.explanation: The negative changes nothing: **used to** still takes **-ing**.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor na tom nic nemění: po **used to** je pořád **-ing**.

items.en: Are you used to your new school yet?
items.cz: Zvykl sis už na novou školu?
items.gap: Are you used to ____ yet? (your new school)
accepts: Are you used to your new school yet?
items.explanation: A noun after **used to** stays a noun — *school*, not schooling.
items.explanation_cz: Podstatné jméno po **used to** zůstane podstatným jménem — *school*, ne schooling.

items.en: He is getting used to his new phone.
items.cz: Zvyká si na nový telefon.
items.gap: He is ____ used to his new phone. (get)
accepts: He is getting used to his new phone.
He's getting used to his new phone.
items.wrong: He is get used to his new phone.
items.explanation: The change is still going on, so **is getting** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Změna pořád probíhá, takže **is getting** used to.

items.en: My parents never got used to living in a city.
items.cz: Rodiče si nikdy nezvykli na život ve městě.
items.gap: My parents never ____ used to living in a city. (get)
accepts: My parents never got used to living in a city.
items.wrong: My parents never get used to living in a city.
items.explanation: **never got** used to = the change never finished. *were* would say they already were.
items.explanation_cz: **never got** used to = ta změna nikdy neproběhla. *were* by říkalo, že už zvyklí byli.

items.en: We are used to working in a big team.
items.cz: Jsme zvyklí pracovat ve velkém týmu.
items.gap: We are used to ____ in a big team. (work)
accepts: We are used to working in a big team.
We're used to working in a big team.
items.wrong: We are used to work in a big team.
items.explanation: **working** — the -ing form after used to, however long the sentence gets.
items.explanation_cz: **working** — tvar s -ing po used to, ať je věta jakkoli dlouhá.

items.en: She used to work in a bank, but now she is a teacher.
items.cz: Dřív pracovala v bance, ale teď je učitelka.
items.gap: She ____ in a bank, but now she is a teacher. (work)
accepts: She used to work in a bank, but now she is a teacher.
She used to work in a bank, but now she's a teacher.
items.wrong: She used to working in a bank, but now she is a teacher.
items.explanation: This is the **past habit** *used to* — plain verb, no be. *She is used to working* would mean it feels normal to her now.
items.explanation_cz: Tohle je *used to* pro **minulý zvyk** — základní tvar, žádné be. *She is used to working* by znamenalo, že jí to teď přijde normální.

items.en: He is used to travelling by train every day.
items.cz: Je zvyklý jezdit každý den vlakem.
items.gap: He is used to ____ by train every day. (travel)
accepts: He is used to travelling by train every day.
He's used to travelling by train every day.
items.wrong: He is used to travel by train every day.
items.explanation: **travelling** after used to. *to travel* is the infinitive, which never follows this *to*.
items.explanation_cz: Po used to je **travelling**. *to travel* je infinitiv, ten po tomhle *to* nikdy nestojí.

items.en: You will soon get used to it.
items.cz: Brzy si na to zvykneš.
items.gap: You will soon ____ used to it. (get)
accepts: You will soon get used to it.
You'll soon get used to it.
items.wrong: You will soon getting used to it.
items.explanation: After **will** the verb is plain: will **get** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Po **will** je základní tvar: will **get** used to.

items.en: They are getting used to speaking Czech.
items.cz: Zvykají si mluvit česky.
items.gap: They are getting used to ____ Czech. (speak)
accepts: They are getting used to speaking Czech.
They're getting used to speaking Czech.
items.wrong: They are getting used to speak Czech.
items.explanation: Even with **getting**, the verb after used to keeps **-ing**: speaking.
items.explanation_cz: I s **getting** zůstává sloveso po used to v **-ing**: speaking.

items.en: I am not used to this weather.
items.cz: Na tohle počasí nejsem zvyklý.
items.gap: I am not used to ____. (this weather)
accepts: I am not used to this weather.
I'm not used to this weather.
items.explanation: A noun needs nothing added — **this weather** is the whole thing after used to.
items.explanation_cz: K podstatnému jménu se nic nepřidává — po used to stojí **this weather** tak, jak je.

items.en: Did you get used to the food?
items.cz: Zvykl sis na to jídlo?
items.gap: Did you ____ used to the food? (get)
accepts: Did you get used to the food?
items.wrong: Did you got used to the food?
items.explanation: After **did** the verb is plain: did you **get** used to.
items.explanation_cz: Po **did** je základní tvar: did you **get** used to.

items.en: She is not used to speaking in front of people.
items.cz: Není zvyklá mluvit před lidmi.
items.gap: She is not used to ____ in front of people. (speak)
accepts: She is not used to speaking in front of people.
She isn't used to speaking in front of people.
items.wrong: She is not used to speak in front of people.
items.explanation: **speaking** — the negative does not change the -ing.
items.explanation_cz: **speaking** — zápor na -ing nic nemění.

items.en: My sister is getting used to her new car.
items.cz: Sestra si zvyká na nové auto.
items.gap: My sister is ____ used to her new car. (get)
accepts: My sister is getting used to her new car.
items.wrong: My sister is got used to her new car.
items.explanation: The change is in progress: **is getting** used to, not is got.
items.explanation_cz: Změna probíhá: **is getting** used to, ne is got.

items.en: He got used to working at night.
items.cz: Zvykl si pracovat v noci.
items.gap: He ____ used to working at night. (get)
accepts: He got used to working at night.
items.wrong: He getting used to working at night.
items.explanation: **got** used to = the change is finished. He is comfortable with it now.
items.explanation_cz: **got** used to = změna proběhla. Teď mu to už nevadí.
